official_measurement_examples.name: Part D scope
official_measurement_examples.fact: Approved Document D addresses toxic substances associated with insulating material inserted into cavity walls and prevention of toxic fumes entering buildings.

official_measurement_examples.name: Not general contamination law
official_measurement_examples.fact: Part D toxic-substance guidance is not a substitute for planning contaminated-land assessment or Approved Document C ground-contamination controls.

official_measurement_examples.name: Cavity insulation self-certification
official_measurement_examples.fact: Government competent-person guidance lists cavity-wall insulation among work that can be covered by authorised self-certification schemes where scope and installer registration apply.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2026 insulation competence
official_measurement_examples.fact: The 1 July 2026 mandatory technical competence framework includes insulation as a competence category for self-certification schemes.

official_measurement_examples.name: Installer status caveat
official_measurement_examples.fact: Scheme membership demonstrates an authorised route to self-certify covered work but does not prove a particular cavity installation was correctly completed.

official_measurement_examples.name: Approval versus standards
official_measurement_examples.fact: Work exempt from advance approval or carried out under a scheme must still meet applicable Building Regulations standards.

official_measurement_examples.name: Energy separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Cavity insulation thermal performance and Part D toxic-fume protection are separate compliance questions.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Part D compliance does not grant planning permission or establish parcel development capacity.

core_rules: Part D compliance is not planning permission
planning permission is not Part D compliance
Part D is not a general contaminated-land regime
Part D cavity-insulation toxicity is distinct from Part C ground contamination
competent-person scheme membership is not proof of a specific installation
self-certification route is not planning approval
no separate application is not the same as no Building Regulations duty
insulation thermal performance is not toxic-fume compliance
product suitability is not proof of correct installation
historic Part D edition must retain its date
MTC framework is competence evidence not parcel approval
cavity insulation presence is not proof of wall suitability
Part D compliance is not a guarantee of indoor-air quality from all sources
Part D compliance does not create ownership or access rights
no parcel toxic-substance clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
